title: US macro resilience coexists with fiscal, external, and financial-stability tail risks
source_unit: IMF 2026 Article IV consultation for the United States; staff estimates, projections, and Executive Board assessment

denominator.unit: IMF Article IV country consultation and selected-indicator framework

interpretive_assessment.value: strong broad-based productivity and policy adaptation alongside elevated debt, current-account deficit, tariff uncertainty, and slower employment growth

observations.method: IMF bilateral Article IV consultation using national accounts, labor, fiscal, external, financial, and policy information; report completed March 17 and discussed by the Executive Board April 1, 2026.
observations.uncertainty: The figures are IMF staff estimates or source-based assessments, not a household survey or firm-level causal design. Q4/Q4 growth, fiscal-year balances, general-government debt, and current-account measures have distinct periods and definitions; the government shutdown and policy changes complicate interpretation.
observations.subgroup: US macroeconomic, fiscal, labor, external, and financial-system aggregates; no household or worker subgroup estimate is supplied in this record.
observations.counterinterpretation: Strong aggregate growth and productivity can coexist with uneven household experience, slower employment growth, or higher financial vulnerability. A high debt ratio is a state-finance risk indicator, not a direct measure of household debt or political legitimacy.

denominator.unit: projection years 2026-2031 in the selected-indicator table

general_government_gross_debt.value: 125.8% of GDP in 2026 rising to 141.5% in 2031

policy_risks.value: tariff passthrough, energy prices, fiscal imbalance, short-maturity debt, external rebalancing, nonbank visibility, and financial-regulatory change

observations.method: IMF staff baseline projection and Executive Board policy assessment in the 2026 United States Article IV report; projections use information available at the consultation date.
observations.uncertainty: Projections are conditional scenarios rather than realized outcomes. They are sensitive to tariffs, energy prices, fiscal legislation, immigration flows, monetary policy, financial conditions, and geopolitical developments; revisions should be preserved as later vintages arrive.
observations.subgroup: US aggregate macroeconomic and public-finance outlook; distributional effects, household incidence, and state-level variation are not estimated here.
observations.counterinterpretation: A projected unemployment rate near 4% does not imply equal job access or worker control, and projected debt growth does not identify which programs, households, or generations bear adjustment costs.

related_sources.claim: IMF eLibrary citation and publication metadata for United States Country Report No. 2026/076.
IMF WEO April 2026 supplies the global defense, conflict, tariff, and fiscal trade-off comparison.
BEA is among the source agencies underlying selected US national-account indicators.

boundary: This record adds an IMF country-surveillance layer to the US atlas. It distinguishes retrospective aggregate conditions from conditional projections and policy assessment. It does not estimate household welfare, worker control, cultural meaning, political response, firm-level incidence, or geopolitical leverage; those arrows require compatible micro, institutional, and state-response evidence.
